=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer-side review

The Seller’s “STANDARD”, “FINAL” and reviewer-efficiency labels are negotiation advocacy, not agreed limitations on our review. Several positions materially shift known transaction risk to Wattlebridge and should be rejected or substantially amended.

### 1. Liability regime is too broad, particularly for fundamental and known risks
**Seller position:** 20% cap ($4.8m), $25,000 de minimis, $250,000 deductible basket, 18-month limit; applies to all claims, including title/capacity; broad exclusive-remedy, limitations and non-reliance provisions.

**Buyer concern / pushback:**
- The regime must **not apply to all claims**. Carve out at minimum:
  - fraud, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment;
  - title to shares, authority/capacity and seller ownership;
  - Tax claims and pre-Completion tax liabilities;
  - debt, security interests and leakage/price-mechanics claims;
  - IP ownership/infringement and the Ironquay issue;
  - the Riverlark facility/security discharge;
  - specific indemnities and covenant claims;
  - breach of Completion deliverables.
- Title/capacity should be subject to a **100% purchase-price cap** (or uncapped for title), not the general $4.8m cap. The Seller’s share register is evidence only; it is not a substitute for a title warranty, transfer documents and no-security protection.
- Tax, title and fundamental warranties require longer survival periods (commonly the applicable statutory limitation period for tax and 5–7 years for fundamental matters). An 18-month period is inadequate for risks that may only emerge after audit, tax assessment or contractual enforcement.
- Claims under special indemnities and price adjustments should be recoverable **dollar-for-dollar**, without the general de minimis, basket, cap or short limitation period.
- For general warranties, the $250,000 deductible basket means Wattlebridge bears the first $250,000 of aggregate loss. At a minimum, negotiate a **tipping basket** once exceeded and resist any qualification that excludes claims merely because they are “discoverable.”
- The general cap should be reconsidered in light of the concentration, debt, IP and incident risks. If 20% is ultimately accepted for ordinary warranties, it cannot be a cap for the excluded categories above.

### 2. Overbroad data-room, public-record and buyer-knowledge disclosures
**Seller position:** Every matter “contained or referred to” in the data room, statutory registers and public records is generally disclosed; no claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable from those sources.

**Buyer concern / pushback:**
- Reject blanket disclosure of the entire data room and public registers. Disclosure should be effective only if it is **fair, specific, accurate and sufficiently detailed** to identify the nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable consequences of the relevant exception to a particular warranty.
- General disclosure cannot turn incomplete documents, missing consents, ambiguous references or a fact that was merely discoverable into disclosure of the actual risk.
- “Knowledge” must mean **actual knowledge of specified senior Buyer deal team members**, not imputed knowledge of all advisers, nor constructive knowledge based on documents that could have been found or interpreted.
- The Seller should warrant that the disclosure letter and data room are complete, accurate and not misleading by omission in all material respects, with an agreed index/snapshot as at signing and an obligation to update through Completion.
- The disclosure date is 22 September 2026. Require a current bring-down disclosure letter and a right to terminate, defer Completion, require a cure, or obtain an indemnity/price adjustment for material new matters.

### 3. Bluefen consent is a critical Completion issue
**Facts disclosed:** Bluefen represents approximately $3.6m FY26 revenue, around 30% of revenue. The agreement has a change-of-control consent provision with conditions; no final written consent or evidence of satisfaction of conditions is available.

**Buyer concern / pushback:**
- This is a material customer-concentration and revenue-continuity risk, not an administrative item.
- Make an **unconditional, effective Bluefen consent**, and satisfaction of all attached conditions, a Buyer-benefit Completion condition. Delivery of a conditional consent must not be deemed satisfaction.
- Wattlebridge must approve the wording and any commercial conditions. No conditions should impose post-Completion cost, service obligations, pricing concessions, releases or other burdens without Buyer approval.
- If the Seller will not make it a condition, require a substantial holdback/escrow or a specific indemnity for all losses arising from absence, invalidity or breach of the consent, plus an express termination right. Given the 30% revenue exposure, a general $4.8m capped claim is not adequate protection.

### 4. Riverlark debt and security must be cleared at Completion, not afterwards
**Facts disclosed:** About $3.2m remains outstanding, subject to a change-of-control provision; there is no repayment or final security discharge.

**Buyer concern / pushback:**
- A debt-free/cash-free transaction requires the facility to be repaid and all related security interests released **at or before Completion**, simultaneously with funds flow.
- Do not accept a release “following Completion.” Completion should require:
  - lender-approved payoff letter;
  - agreed amount and payment direction in the funds flow;
  - irrevocable release documentation effective on receipt of payoff funds;
  - discharge/withdrawal of every registered and unregistered security interest, guarantee and cross-default exposure; and
  - evidence of PPSR releases as soon as registrable.
- If a release is not delivered at Completion, Buyer should be entitled to withhold the relevant funds or defer/terminate Completion. The full debt repayment and discharge risk must sit with Seller, not the Company or Buyer.

### 5. Ironquay IP requires a real solution, not a narrow payment indemnity
**Facts disclosed:** Transfer of SOW3 project materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; $180,000 is shown open, with no independent confirmation, receipt or confirmatory assignment.

**Buyer concern / pushback:**
- This may leave the Company without ownership of key development materials, or exposed to infringement/termination claims. The dollar amount of the outstanding invoice does not measure the value of the affected IP.
- Require before Completion:
  - proof of payment/settlement acceptable to Buyer;
  - an unconditional confirmatory assignment of all relevant IP and project materials to the Company;
  - waivers of retention, termination and lien rights;
  - moral-rights consents where relevant; and
  - an IP chain-of-title schedule.
- Alternatively, require a specific, uncapped (or appropriately high) indemnity and escrow, covering loss of use, replacement/redevelopment costs, infringement claims and business interruption—not merely the SOW3 payment.

### 6. Completion bonuses are potentially undisclosed debt/leakage
**Facts disclosed:** Conditional Completion bonuses total $420,000, excluded from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unknown.

**Buyer concern / pushback:**
- These are transaction-linked liabilities and potentially seller leakage, not merely a Seller-side matter. Their conditional character does not make the post-Completion cost disappear.
- Require the Seller to pay them before Completion, or deduct/withhold the full liability from the purchase price. The amount must include superannuation, payroll tax, leave impacts, payroll processing and all other on-costs.
- Obtain a detailed schedule identifying recipients, terms, approvals, accrued amounts and tax treatment, together with a specific indemnity for all bonus-related liabilities.
- Ensure no employee has an undisclosed change-of-control, retention, acceleration, severance or termination entitlement.

### 7. Export/privacy incident needs a Completion condition or tailored indemnity
**Facts disclosed:** An export link may have been sent to an unintended external address and may contain approximately 1,240 records; access, scope and notification obligations are unresolved.

**Buyer concern / pushback:**
- The absence of confirmed access or quantified loss is not comfort. The risk includes regulatory notification, investigation, remediation, customer claims, contractual breaches, reputational damage and future costs.
- Require a properly scoped forensic investigation, preservation of evidence, containment/revocation of access, documented risk assessment, and legal advice on notification obligations before Completion.
- Require Seller not to communicate with affected people, customers or regulators without Buyer approval (except where legally required), and to keep Buyer fully informed.
- Make resolution to Buyer’s satisfaction a Completion condition, or obtain a **specific indemnity outside general limitations**, with an escrow/holdback sized to the credible exposure. General warranty survival of 18 months may also be insufficient for regulatory matters.

### 8. Contract notices, consents and supplier renewals need verification
**Office lease / Mossvale**
- The disclosures seek to characterise notice and assignment provisions narrowly. Require the actual clauses and counterparty confirmation where there is any doubt.
- A share sale can trigger “change in control,” deemed assignment, notice, termination or default wording even if it is not technically an assignment. Obtain required notices, waivers and consents before Completion, or protect through a condition/indemnity.

**Sandbar supplier renewals**
- Three renewals totalling $330,000 cannot simply be labelled ordinary course without evidence.
- Require contracts, renewal dates, term/termination rights, payment status, approval history and evidence they were entered into in the ordinary course and consistently with past practice.
- Add a no-extraordinary-commitments covenant from signing to Completion and prevent renewals, amendments or commitments above agreed thresholds without Buyer consent.
- If the costs relate to periods after Completion, ensure they are correctly treated in working capital/debt/leakage mechanics and not disguised seller liabilities.

### 9. Warranties must remain meaningful
The Seller’s proposal to put tax and IP “under the general regime,” coupled with broad disclosure and constructive-knowledge wording, could leave Wattlebridge with little effective recourse.

**Push for:**
- robust unqualified warranties on title, authority, accounts, no undisclosed liabilities, debt/security, tax, IP ownership/non-infringement, material contracts, data protection/cybersecurity, employment and compliance;
- no warranty qualification by data-room disclosure except specifically and fairly disclosed matters;
- a bring-down of warranties at Completion;
- Seller pre-Completion covenants to operate in the ordinary course, preserve key contracts/IP/data, and notify Buyer promptly of material developments;
- remedies that are cumulative, with the SPA’s exclusive-remedy wording limited to contractual warranty claims and preserving the identified carve-outs.

## Recommended priority positions

1. **Completion protection:** unconditional Bluefen consent; Riverlark payoff and security releases simultaneous with Completion; Ironquay IP cure; and full accounting/treatment of the $420,000 bonuses and on-costs.  
2. **Risk allocation:** specific indemnities/escrows, outside general caps and time limits, for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses and the privacy incident.  
3. **Limitations:** no general cap/time limit for title, tax, debt/security, IP, fraud, special indemnities, Completion deliverables or price claims; longer survival for fundamental/tax matters.  
4. **Disclosure and knowledge:** remove blanket data-room/public-record disclosure and constructive knowledge; require specific fair disclosure, actual named-person knowledge and updated disclosure through Completion.  
5. **Further diligence/contract protection:** verify all change-of-control, lease, Mossvale and supplier-contract consequences; require no adverse action or new commitments before Completion without Buyer consent.

On the material presently disclosed, Wattlebridge should not accept the Seller’s package as a “balanced” allocation: it transfers several identified, potentially transaction-threatening risks to Buyer while materially restricting Buyer’s recourse.
